reason: The claim's citation does not support it at the scope asserted: I fetched https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md directly and it contains no mention of a "most restrictive answer" combination rule for conflicting PreToolUse decisions (the word "restrictive" appears nowhere on the page, and there is no section on merging conflicting decisions across matching hooks) — the page documents parallel execution and cross-level merging of hook *entries*, but not how conflicting *decisions* are resolved. The repo's own harness-survey.md carries that exact "most restrictive answer" mechanic in a separate row ("Combining results from multiple matching hooks") sourced to a different URL, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md, not hooks.md — so the claim cites the wrong page for the fact its whole argument depends on. Independently, the repo's own audit ledger already records this exact item: harness-survey.md lists "PreToolUse branch guard" under both the Claude Code module table and the Mechanisms table with disposition COMPLEMENT (native feature "PreToolUse hook ... and multi-hook result combination") and action reword-to-cite-native-floor, not CONFLICT/resolve-conflict as the claim proposes. This matches the guard script's own header comment (plugins/house/hooks/no-direct-master.sh, lines 28-32), which already states "every matching PreToolUse hook still runs and the most restrictive decision wins, so this deferral is a deliberate migration choice here, not something the harness requires" — i.e. the rule's authors already account for the harness's multi-hook merging when designing the deferral, so the claim's "surrenders enforcement" framing describes a known, documented design choice, not an undiscovered conflict.
citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md (fetched directly: no "most restrictive wins" combination rule appears on this page; that content is instead sourced by the repo's own docs/handbook/sources/harness-survey.md to https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide.md)
